title: The Chu Berry automobile accident near Youngstown
summary: On the road to Toronto the bus came on Lamar Wright's overturned car; Chu Berry was injured with a skull fracture and was delirious.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But, you know, one of the greatest things that I'll never forget with that band -- of course, there was so many great things happened even when I first come into the band the changes that went on in the band and everything. I'll never forget the night that poor Choo, that we was on the way from Youngstown, Ohio, --
Youngstown going to Buffalo, going to Canada.

-- to get going to Toronto, and Lamar had his car -- he wanted to drive this car up to show off up in Toronto 'cause he had a friend up there, you know -- and so the bus driver that we had he got killed in Saipan, Billy.
So they left ahead of us and it was a very slick road, very slick road up in northern Ohio. They

had those brick roads. And so we was coming up the highway and all at once we see the car turned over in the road and we see these three guys sitting out there. So the bus driver, he said, "Do you know," he said, "that looks like [ ]".
That's right. Yeah, that was our nickname for him. I don't know how he got it because it was there before I came to the band.

So Calloway said, "Don't say that," you know, and so when we got up there, really, the car had turned over, Lamar Wright was sitting there and Brown was sitting there and Chu Choo was sitting there but he was talking out of his head.
They had already -- a truck had already sent for the ambulance when we got there.

And they brought Chu Choo around to sit in front of the bus, you know, until the ambulance came, and Chu Choo kept on repeating -- and I found out later what he was saying and who he was talking about -- he said, "Baby, I don't have no more." I knew the chick in Chicago. She was begging for bread. And Chu Choo said, "I don't have no more." That's who he was talking about, I found out way late.
So then they got him to the hospital and he was out of his head. He was bleeding out of his ear because he had a
fracture at the base of his skull.
Yes, his skull was crushed on one side.

That's right. And he got to the hospital, and Cnd Choo was an enormous man. He weighed 260, you know, and was all man. Do you remember the time that he was playing with Calloway and he took Calloway by the arm and took him all the way down the back of the bus.
He told Calloway, 'Don't fool with me,' you know.
